newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK IN TALKS WITH JAPANESE CARMAKER.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK IN TALKS WITH JAPANESE CARMAKER.

text.p: VSZ a.s., Slovakia's largest steel maker said on Monday it was in preliminary negotiations with an unspecified Japanese carmaker on building a car assembly plant in Slovakia.
"We are negotiating with (Japanese) Nomura Bank....but these talks are still only very preliminary," Jan Seno, VSZ Vice President for finance told Reuters.
VSZ has often said that setting up a car assembly plant in Slovakia is part of its long-term strategy to diversify steel output to more sophisticated products with a higher added value.
Two years ago it began talks on a plant with Korean KIA car producer, but the talks ended without a resolution.
Last month VSZ Supervisory Board Chairman Alexander Rezes said VSZ was preparing extensive restructuring measures, partly in the hope of forging ties with Japan's Toyota Motor Corp.
After a trip to Japan at the beginning of April, Finance Minister Sergei Kozlik said Toyota was considering locating a car produciton plant in eastern Slovakia.
Toyota has so far not commented on the project.
VSZ Director Jan Smerek said on Monday the company planned to strengthen its focus on non-steel production sectors.
"We want to focus more strongly on other sectors such as banking, automobile produciton and services," Smerek said.

VSZ is already diversifying into other fields in order to offset the cyclical nature of the steel industry, and has heavily invested in the past two years into banking, insurance, services and even sports teams.
Last year VSZ invested 2.5 billion crowns into its main steel production which, Smerek said, was a sufficient amount.
Investments in 1997 are estimated at 3.5 billion crowns of which the major part will go to the production of zinc-coated sheet steel.
